verdict.rationale: Stripe documents several pieces of headless, scriptable operation. There is a CLI to build, test and manage integrations from the command line, and API-key authentication for integrations. Coding agents can also provision an anonymous sandbox with working API keys from the CLI, with no account registration, plus restricted keys for least-privilege automation. Missing for 10: explicit CI/CD pipeline documentation (e.g., GitHub Actions or non-interactive CLI auth guidance), and independent or hands-on corroboration of headless CI runs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Build, test, and manage your Stripe integration from the command line.

Coding agents should install the Stripe CLI (npm i -g @stripe/cli) and run the command stripe sandbox create --help to provision an anonymous Stripe sandbox with working API keys. No account registration required.
Stripe uses API keys to authenticate requests from your integration and determine which Stripe resources it can access.
Use RAK permissions to limit what an agent can do in your account.
